keyFindings.description: legionagents.Open failing is log.Fatal: a listener image released before the envoy-infra grant lands crash-loops every listener (all Envoy delivery and role routing on that host) for a display-only registry, and the PR carries no Contract change census for this new start-up refusal at the listener/NATS-grant boundary. Degrade instead (log ERROR, keep the store nil, /v1/legion/agents* answer 503, reopen on the reconnect hook), which Dispatch already handles as legion_registry unavailable.

prepare reads session.<id>, then write does three plain kv.Put calls: two concurrent writes of one session with different issues, or a write that dies after its index keys followed by a re-put with another issue, both pass and leave index keys under two issues, breaking the stated 409 / no-orphaned-index guarantee with no delete route to repair it. Claim with kv.Create (new) or kv.Update at the read revision (re-put) before writing index keys.
Store.list copies kvwatch.ScanExistingKeys' end-of-scan protocol (nil marker, idleTimeout on Error(), closed channel); generalise the kvwatch helper (filter and watch options) and use it.
The closed rule is a bare bool through six functions, and here `suggestion` is passed as refuseClosed; separate the lock read from the refusal or use a named type.

Title doc says 'newest stamped title' but ResolveSessionTitles returns the newest event's title and null when that event carries none (tester observation 1); correct here, in contracts dispatch-api.ts:1580 and cmd/dispatch/AGENTS.md:440.
Says a reopen of an existing comment stays 409 on a closed issue, but a reply to a resolved root reopens it there (plan D2, tester-confirmed); same in packages/envoy/AGENTS.md:1902.
reportQuoteComment swallows the host's 'The selection holds no text to quote.' error, so Comment silently does nothing; and its `quote` field is computed and never used by the host.
The batch PUT sends bus.ErrRefused to the 503 retry branch while the single PUT answers it 4xx; route both through writeLegionAgentError with a typed partial-write error.
getIssueCollaborators and the four web type re-exports have no caller after spec v4 moved the tab to INFRA-470: dead code left by the cutover.

observationsJudged: Tester observation 1 (null title): code behaviour accepted (the registry title wins for Legion agents and plugin writes always stamp one); the doc that contradicts it is finding 5.

Tester observation 2 (registry writable by any /v1 bearer): not a defect of this PR: same flat /v1 trust as /v1/roles/set, the registry is display-only here and INFRA-204's daemon answers only sessions its own history holds; recorded under Not proven / risk.
Tester observation 3 (live follows the 5-minute session TTL): not a defect: it is the listener's live rule everywhere, and the collaborators route carries no running flag (plan D4).
